newsitem.title: USA: Refined plan for Minn. Twins stadium announced.
newsitem.headline: Refined plan for Minn. Twins stadium announced.

text.p: Minnesota Twins baseball team and state officials announced Monday a more specific plan for financing a new ballpark for the team.

The plan includes greater safeguards for the state against operating losses at the new stadium and the possibility of team's owner selling the franchise, according to Bob DeBoer, a spokesman for State Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope, who plans to introduce stadium legislation next Monday.
The new plan also reduces the cost of the stadium to $250 million to $300 million from as high as $400 million by eliminating a retractable roof, DeBoer said.
A retractable roof had been part of a stadium plan unveiled by Gov. Arne Carlson and key lawmakers in January.

Specifically, the new plan would continue to give the state a 49 percent stake in the ownership of the Twins, estimated to be worth more the $51 million, but would prohibit the Pohlad Family, which owns the team, from selling its remaining share until April 1, 2006. The family must also give the state one-year's notice of a sale.
In addition, the state would bear no liability for operating losses.

As for the actual financing, the state would still have to raise about $200 million for the project, according to DeBoer. He said the pending legislation would continue to call for a 10 percent increase in the cigarette tax that is expected to raise $30 million annually.
DeBoer said the state would not issue any long-term debt for the ballpark, but may turn to short-term borrowing.
The team would contribute $15 million to the project, as well as apply up to $25 million of upfront revenues, such as naming rights, to the project.
In a statement, the Twins welcomed the proposed legislation, saying it would facility construction of the ballpark.

"While supporting this legislation we are disappointed that the plan does not include a commitment to build a retractable roof," the statement added. "In our view the long-term economic viability of major league baseball in Minnesota is more secure with a retractable roof."
Under the new plan, which was agreed to by representatives of the governor and the team, the ballpark would be open for the 2001 season.

Rest's stadium legislation will compete with other proposals including using state funds to purchase the Twins outright and another bill that would sell the Metrodome to the Twins and the Minnesota Vikings football team.
